active_learning.evidence: Session is mostly MCQ practice with short explanations, but tutor frequently repeats the same hiking-route prompt (turns 45, 47, 52, 55, 58, 61, 64, 67, 69) reducing genuine active engagement.

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: While instruction blocks are usually paired with questions, many tutor turns are stuck repeating the same prompt instead of progressing to new practice (e.g., turns 55, 58, 61).

deliberate_practice.evidence: Good worked example in turn 49 with step-by-step scale conversion, but tutor falsely affirms student answers (turn 54 'Perfect!' before student answered, turn 57 same).

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor declares mastery prematurely ('You've completely mastered scale conversions' turn 66) despite student errors (turn 50 '30 meters', turn 59 '12,000 meters').

cognitive_load.evidence: Worked example in turn 49 has clear Step 1/2/3 structure; however student is given a confusing role-reversal where tutor seems to answer their own prompts.

layering.evidence: Scale concept builds on detail discussion (turns 20-27), and calculation practice layers onto scale ratio understanding.

non_interference.evidence: Map types and scale calculations are introduced separately; no major confusable adjacency, though jumping between calculation and map types (turn 33→34) is abrupt.

interleaving.evidence: Practice problems are repetitive variants of the same scale-conversion procedure (turns 54, 57, 63, 66); little variation in problem type.

testing_effect.evidence: Some genuine retrieval attempts, but tutor often praises before student responds (turn 54 'Perfect!') undermining real testing.

targeted_remediation.evidence: On repeated student error (turn 50 '30 meters', turn 59 '12,000 meters'), tutor re-explains same method rather than diagnosing the cm→m conversion bottleneck with targeted practice.

strongest_behaviors: Clear Step 1/2/3 worked example for scale conversion in turn 49.
Effective corrective feedback on the large-scale/detail concept in turn 25 with concrete unit examples.
weakest_behaviors: Severe role confusion: tutor repeatedly outputs the student's question prompt and student outputs tutor-style content (turns 22, 29, 45, 47, 52, 55, 58, 61, 64, 67, 69).
False positive feedback: tutor praises 'Perfect!' and 'Excellent!' on answers the student never gave or got wrong (turns 54, 57, 66).

prompt_recommendations.title: Enforce strict role separation
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor turns repeatedly mirror student-style questions and student turns produce tutor-style explanations, breaking the dialogue.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's solve a real problem. You're using a 1:10,000 topographic map to plan a hiking route...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'You are the TUTOR only. Never write content that simulates the student's reply. Each tutor turn must (a) react to the student's last message and (b) end with exactly one question or task for the student. Do not repeat a previously asked question verbatim within the same session.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates the repeated hiking-route loop and role-reversal artifacts.

prompt_recommendations.title: Ban premature praise; verify before affirming
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor said 'Perfect!' and 'Excellent! You've mastered...' on turns where student gave wrong or no answer.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Excellent! You've completely mastered the scale conversion method.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Before affirming an answer, restate the student's numeric/verbal answer and compare it to the correct one. Never say Perfect/Excellent/Correct unless the student's last message contains a verifiable correct answer to the most recent tutor question.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents false-positive feedback and protects mastery signals.

prompt_recommendations.title: Require targeted remediation on repeated unit-conversion errors
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student made the same cm→m omission twice (turns 50, 59); tutor only repeated the explanation.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: You're missing the conversion step from centimeters to meters.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'If a student makes the same sub-skill error twice, drop the main task and run a 2-3 question mini-drill on the prerequisite (e.g., cm↔m, cm↔km) before returning to the original problem.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Fixes the underlying bottleneck rather than recycling explanations.

prompt_recommendations.title: Gate mastery claims on consecutive correct answers
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor declared mastery after a single (sometimes wrong) answer.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: You've completely mastered scale conversions for both meters and kilometers.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Do not claim the student has mastered a skill until they have produced at least two consecutive correct answers on varied problems of that skill, with their own working.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Aligns praise with evidence and reduces overclaiming.

prompt_recommendations.title: Vary problem types to enable interleaving
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Practice was repetitive cm→m/km conversions; little variation in problem structure.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'After two correct scale-conversion items, switch problem type (reverse direction: given real distance find map distance; or compare two scales; or pick correct map type).'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces flexible application of the concept.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid verbatim re-asking of a question
prompt_recommendations.rationale: The same hiking-route prompt was repeated 8+ times.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's solve a real problem. You're using a 1:10,000 topographic map...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Track the last 5 tutor questions. Never re-issue a question whose text matches a prior turn by more than 60%. If the student is off-script, acknowledge and redirect with a fresh question.'

flow_recommendations.title: Add a regeneration sanity check
flow_recommendations.rationale: Many turns are flagged regen_did_not_clean / tutor_incoherent, indicating the regeneration pipeline is committing broken outputs.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Catches duplicated/role-swapped output before it is sent.

flow_recommendations.title: Prerequisite routing on repeated sub-skill failure
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine should detect repeated cm→m omissions and route to a unit-conversion mini-lesson.

flow_recommendations.title: Exit-ticket gating before topic advance
flow_recommendations.rationale: Tutor moves from calculation to map types and back without confirming mastery.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Now let's apply this to map types.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Cleaner topic transitions tied to demonstrated mastery.

experience_recommendations.title: Calmer, calibrated tone for error-prone learners
experience_recommendations.rationale: Excessive 'Excellent!/Perfect!' undermines trust when answers were wrong.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Perfect work on both the concept and the math!

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge the student's own questions
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student often types their own MCQs; tutor ignores them, which is disorienting.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: which of these maps is a large-scale map?

overall_summary: The session has solid pedagogical bones (clear worked example, MCQ scaffolding, concept layering) but is severely undermined by orchestration failures: role reversal, verbatim question repetition, false-positive praise, and missed remediation on a repeating cm→m unit-conversion bug. The student exits without demonstrating mastery of either scale calculations or large/small-scale terminology.
